assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a physical idea with a clear underlying principle (thermodynamics of demixing, scaling of condensate formation) that reframed how cells compartmentalize without membranes. Original discovery with broad generative reach across cell biology, disease and synthetic biology; easy to explain to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the founding 2009 P-granule observation and its physical interpretation; Rosen supplied the quantitative multivalent-interaction framework on reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag are important on sequence grammar but the discovery of the principle is best captured by the first three.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups over 15+ years, though the interpretation is still debated for specific in vivo condensates; the core principle is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Debate over whether many reported condensates are true equilibrium phase separation versus other assemblies.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry or cell biology/biophysics.
Credit split between founding observation and the physical-chemistry framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation is a new capability: small molecules that recruit E3 ligases to destroy targets, with PROTACs as a design strategy and molecular glues explained mechanistically. Clear mechanism, quantitative pharmacology, and exactly the kind of previously unforeseen opportunity in drug discovery that the committee likes to highlight.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underpins molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so the three-person cut is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials with convincing independent validation of the concept, but no approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge; recognition is plausible but could be a little early.
uncertainties: Whether clinical outcomes are needed before recognition.
Attribution split between PROTAC concept and molecular-glue mechanism, and the role of Ito and Ciulli.
Exact current clinical status is from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules by the ionic current blockade in a nanopore is a physically elegant measurement, built on single-molecule electrical detection and engineered protein pores. It created a real-time long-read sequencing technology and a general platform for sensing, with clear impact.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the concept, Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation, Bayley engineered pores, and Akeson showed base discrimination and enzyme-controlled ratcheting. Credit is spread across at least five people, which complicates the three-name limit; I would anchor on concept, pore engineering and enzymatic ratcheting.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercially mature and widely validated across independent labs, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether some of the pioneers are deceased or otherwise unavailable; I cannot verify this.
Fair division between concept (Deamer, Branton), first demonstration (Kasianowicz) and sequencing realization (Akeson, Bayley).
Whether this fits chemistry rather than physics or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned an unusual semiconductor into a solar absorber with power conversion efficiencies approaching those of silicon in a little over a decade, with defect tolerance and tunable band gaps that raise real physics questions. A rapid, transformative materials story with large energy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park made the first solid-state high-efficiency device, and Snaith demonstrated meso-superstructured and planar thin-film devices. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also important, so the split is contested.
assessment.maturity: Very strong independent confirmation of efficiencies; long-term stability and commercial deployment are not yet settled, which argues for waiting.
uncertainties: Stability and manufacturing remain open.
Contested credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and others.
Recent chemistry Nobel for MOFs may weigh against another materials-energy prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure calculations with ab initio dynamics in one scheme, allowing chemical reactions and condensed-phase systems to be simulated from first principles. The method has a clear principle and has had decades of impact across chemistry, materials and biology.
assessment.attribution: A two-person 1985 paper with unambiguous credit; a clean prize configuration. Parrinello's later metadynamics and ML potentials could complicate the citation if the committee prefers one broader computational prize.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of independent use and validation; the work is highly mature, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: Computational chemistry was recognized in 2013 and DFT in 1998, so the committee may see the area as already covered.
Possible overlap with metadynamics and machine-learned potentials candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the bond structure of individual molecules with a CO-functionalized tip in noncontact AFM is a physically beautiful, quantitative result that lets chemists see bonds, reaction products and on-surface synthesis intermediates directly. Opens new capability in single-molecule chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor and high-resolution frequency-modulation AFM; Gross and Meyer made the 2009 CO-tip molecular-structure breakthrough. Eigler and Ho are pioneers of STM manipulation, which belongs to a different earlier achievement and could muddy the citation.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced widely since 2009; mature, though the 1986 STM Nobel in physics may be seen as precedent.
uncertainties: Whether it reads as chemistry or physics.
Separating AFM instrument development from the molecular imaging result.
Role of STM manipulation pioneers in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami made it possible to build arbitrary nanoscale shapes with near-molecular precision, a design principle that has spawned a large field of programmable nanostructures and nanomachines. It connects directly to my interest in artificial molecular machines.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami is the decisive invention; Shih and Yin extended it to three dimensions and to tile and brick architectures. Seeman, the field founder, died in 2021 and cannot be recognized, and Winfree and Yan are also strong claimants.
assessment.maturity: Field is mature technically but applications beyond research tools are still emerging, so impact is arguably less proven than for others.
uncertainties: Applications remain limited relative to the promise.
Credit among Rothemund, Winfree, Yan, Shih and Yin is hard to resolve.
Whether the Seeman legacy is a reason to hold off.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors carry out chemical conversion of one base to another on DNA without double-strand breaks, an inventive chemistry-led advance with direct therapeutic reach. It is a clear, original design, though conceptually builds on CRISPR, already recognized in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors. Kondo and Nishida independently developed a related cytidine deaminase editor, and Liu also appears in the prime-editing candidate, so the citation would need care.
assessment.maturity: First base-edited therapies are in clinical use or trials, but long-term safety data are limited; recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a combined base and prime editing citation.
Independent related work by Nishida and Kondo.
Trainee versus principal investigator credit.
